subject: Acme probe: comparative performance & cost testing vs CloudBridge — proposed plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.io>
To: Sasha Li <sasha.li@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Jan 2028 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + proposed probe tests (cost/latency)

Hi Sasha — thanks again for a great demo earlier. Quick written recap and a concrete next step so we can align on an apples-to-apples probe with CloudBridge.

Summary of Acme asks from the call:
- Goal: pick the most predictable inference stack for low-latency robotics control + cheaper bulk async labeling.
- Targets you gave: 95th percentile latency < 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens); sustained throughput ~250 req/s for batch workloads; clear per-1M token economics for steady-state inference.
- Compliance: audit logs and VPC support are mandatory.

Proposed 1-week probe (what Redwood will run vs CloudBridge):
1) 1M-token run for both providers with your sample workload (mixed short + medium prompts). We will report cost per 1M tokens, median/95/99 latency, GPU utilization, and effective batch sizes.
2) Cache-hit sensitivity: run same workload with prefix caching enabled/disabled to show cost delta at 20/50/80% hit rates.
3) Batching/throughput sweep: measure per-request latency vs throughput curve (1–500 req/s) to find the knee.

Deliverables: CSV with per-run metrics, PDF summary, and a short script you can re-run. Attaching initial demo metrics we captured from today for baseline.

Ask: Can you confirm the sample dataset (same prompts we used) and let us know if you want CloudBridge included in the same window (we can coordinate with their rep) or run staggered? Also share any procurement constraints/timing.

If this works I’ll loop in Sean to coordinate infra and Marissa to own the results deck.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.io
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: acme-demo-metrics.csv (CSV - 42 KB)

From: Sasha Li <sasha.li@acmerobotics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.io>
Cc: CloudBridge Sales <sales@cloudbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed probe tests (cost/latency)

Thanks Ben — that plan looks solid. A few clarifications:
- We need the per-1M tokens number to include all infra overhead (routing, prefix cache misses, and any model discrepancy adjustments). Total landed price is what procurement will see.
- For latency targets: the 120ms 95th is for onboard short prompts only; for async labeling we care more about cost per 1M tokens for runs of 1–10M tokens.
- CloudBridge said they can run in-parallel but want a 48‑hour overlap window for fair traffic shaping.

Procurement timeline: procurement wants pricing and an SOW by Jan 20 to commit to a Feb pilot.

Go ahead and schedule the runs — staggered is okay if it’s easier, but please keep the overlap as long as you can.

Sasha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.io>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 07:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + proposed probe tests (pricing template + cache plan)

Ben / Sean — quick notes from product/pricing POV before we spin up infra: 

Pricing template suggestions (to be delivered as PDF):
- Line item A: model inference (per-1M tokens) — specify base model unit price and any quantization adjustment.
- Line item B: cache delta credit (report cost at 20/50/80% effective hit rate) so procurement can see savings banding.
- Line item C: bursting/overage policy for Dedicated vs Hosted — show sample math for 1M tokens and 10M tokens.
- Line item D: routing/fallback risk premium — what happens if we fall back to a cheaper model variant.

Test plan additions:
- Add a 'warm-up window' (10k tokens) to get steady KV cache state before measuring.
- Capture both per-request and aggregated token-level cost; include distribution percentiles (p50/p95/p99).

I’ll draft the template and the short PDF summary. Sean — can you add a metric for effective batch size and queue time per request? I want a single-row CSV per run with these columns: run_id, provider, model, tokens_total, tokens_cached, cache_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, gpu_util_pct.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product — Inference Economics, Redwood Inference
